questions.q: What was the one non-negotiable step in this capstone, according to the wrap-up?
options: Lesson 8's health-check query
Lesson 7's actual, tested point-in-time restore — the one thing Overlook's original maintenance plan never did
Lesson 3's deployment of the Azure SQL Database
Lesson 2's written schedule
questions.explain: The real restore test is what separates this project from the untested maintenance plan that started it — it's the one step that couldn't be skipped or merely described.

questions.q: Which of these does the lesson explicitly name as still missing from this beginner project?
options: A written runbook
A backup schedule for the database
High availability/geo-replication, automated alerting, and coverage beyond one database
Any form of restore test
questions.explain: The project is honest about its boundaries: no HA/geo-replication, no automated alerting, and only one database covered — all deliberately out of scope, not oversights.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say naming what's still missing is itself 'part of professional scoping'?
options: Because listing missing features is required for healthcare compliance audits
Because incomplete projects are always preferable to complete ones
Because honestly stating a project's boundaries is the same skill Lesson 1 taught when turning a vague ask into a specific requirement
Because Azure requires every project plan to list unfinished work
questions.explain: Scoping isn't just deciding what's in a project — it's also honestly naming what's deliberately left out, the same discipline Lesson 1 established at the start.

questions.q: What does the Intermediate-tier capstone pick up from, according to the wrap-up?
options: The same single-department recoverability problem, repeated at larger scale
A rebuild of the same backup plan using on-prem SQL Server instead of Azure SQL Database
A completely unrelated fictional company with no connection to Overlook
This project's foundation, moving from 'can we get the data back' to 'can the system keep up, with two departments sharing it'
questions.explain: The Intermediate project builds on this one's backup discipline while introducing a performance and multi-department sharing problem — a genuinely different, harder question.

questions.q: According to the recap, what did Lesson 4 actually confirm, rather than create?
options: Azure's automated full backup, and why BACKUP DATABASE doesn't apply to Azure SQL Database
The database's firewall rules
The health-check query's baseline result
A brand-new full backup triggered manually via T-SQL
questions.explain: Consistent with the PaaS trade-off covered throughout the project, Lesson 4's job was confirming the automated full backup already existed, not creating one by hand.
